content.comment_body: Hello, Is it feasible to combine output modules powered by 24V and 230V in the same configuration?

You can use modules with relay outputs. These relays support both AC230V and DC24V, allowing you to adjust the potential for each output. Regards, [user_name]. I realized you were referring to the power supply rather than the outputs.

This isn't directly possible. 230V expansion modules are compatible only with 230V [product_name] bases or other 230V expansion modules. Similarly, 24V expansion modules should be connected only with 24V [product_name] bases, or analog expansion modules. The only way to combine 230V and 24V extension modules is by placing an analog expansion module between them.

[user_name]: Yes, I have a [product_name] 12 / 24RCE, and also have DM8 230R / DM16 230R from a previous project. I thought that communication between modules was galvanically isolated from the power supply. [user_name]: Thanks.

No, that's not correct. Only analog modules provide potential separation on the left side of the bus, but not on the right. Digital modules do not offer potential separation. This is why combining digital modules with different voltage levels should be avoided.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are discussing whether output modules with different power supply voltages can be used together in a modular system. There is some uncertainty regarding the galvanic isolation between module communication and their power supply, as well as the specifics of mixing 24V and 230V modules without causing electrical issues. The exchange clarifies that digital expansion modules do not have potential separation, impacting system design flexibility.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that combining output modules with both 24V and 230V supplies is possible, assuming communication between modules is isolated from the power source. They are seeking explanation about the proper connection methods.
